NCP-SP Chief Sharad Pawar leaves after being discharged from the Ruby Hall Clinic after two days under medical observation following complaints of pleuritic pain, in Pune. File | Photo Credit: ANI
NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar was admitted to a hospital in Mumbai on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), hours after he was discharged from a multi-speciality healthcare centre in Pune for further tests.
Mr. Pawar's daughter and Baramati MP Supriya Sule said in a social media post that her father has been admitted to Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai.
Earlier in the day, the 85-year-old veteran politician was discharged from Ruby Hall Clinic in Pune, where he was admitted on November 2, following complaints of cough and pleuritic (chest) pain.
After Mr. Pawar was admitted to Ruby Hall Clinic, Sule said he was undergoing medical tests and his health parameters were stable.
Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to Pawar over the phone and enquired about his health as the veteran leader was discharged from Ruby Hall Clinic, his aide said.
The Prime Minister advised Mr. Pawar to take complete rest, Mr. Pawar's aide Vitthal Maniyar said.
"Prime Minister Narendra Modi called Pawar saheb this morning to enquire about his health. He spoke to him with great affection and respect and requested him to take complete rest. Modi told him that Supriya [Sule] was now ready and she and others would take care of the country, while Pawar saheb should rest," Mr. Maniyar told reporters.
Mr. Pawar thanked the prime minister for enquiring about his health, he said.
"Pawar saheb told the PM that he was taking rest and had no worry about the country as all of them were there to take care of things. He thanked Modi for his concern," the aide said.
Dr. Purvez K Grant, chief cardiologist, chairman and managing trustee of Ruby Hall Clinic, had said that Pawar had been admitted for a general check-up and medical observation following complaints of pleuritic pain.
Pleuritic pain refers to chest pain that typically worsens while breathing, coughing or sneezing.
